title: Visitor, Iterator and Memento
idea: Visitor adds operations to a class family without editing it; Iterator walks a collection without exposing its shape; Memento saves an object's state for restoring later.
points: A visitor has one method per node class; each node calls it from `accept`.
In JavaScript, `*[Symbol.iterator]` makes an object work with `for...of` and spread.
A memento is a snapshot that, by agreement, only its creator reads.
A caretaker stores mementos for undo but never looks inside them.

code.title: Iterator and Visitor
code.caption: Write a `CountVisitor` that returns 1 for files and 0 for folders, then sum it.

walk.text: Each node class has `accept`, which calls the visitor method for its own type.
The generator yields the folder, then every child; `yield*` descends into subfolders.
`ListVisitor` formats each node. It is one operation, kept in one class.
`SizeVisitor` adds a second operation without editing `File` or `Folder`.
`for...of` uses the iterator; the caller never needs to touch `items`.
A fresh loop over the same root starts a new walk from the top.

code.title: Memento
code.caption: Save a second memento after typing ', world', type more, then restore twice.

walk.text: The editor's text is private. Nothing outside can set it directly.
`save` returns a frozen snapshot; `restore` is the only way back in.
`History` stacks mementos for undo and never reads their contents.
Save, keep typing, then restore the saved text.

pitfalls: Avoid Visitor when node classes change often; each new class edits every visitor.
Never add or remove items while iterating; collect the changes, then apply them.
Snapshot copies, not references; a memento holding a shared array changes later.

quiz.why: Each spread calls `[Symbol.iterator]` again and gets a fresh generator, so the second spread is not exhausted. The loop stops before `b`.

takeaway: Visitor adds operations, Iterator hides structure, Memento keeps undo points.
